title: A Contact for the Ghost
premise: Emrys Delacroix, a whistle-blower who has survived by erasing herself, is hired to trace a missing passenger list when Flight 447's records vanish mid-air. The trail leads to a memory-clinic network that wipes witnesses of a weapons transfer, and to a scheduled 'accident' meant to bury the last living insider. Emrys must recover her own erased memories to identify the target, expose the network, and stop the attack — choosing at last to exist under her real name, even as the people who taught her to disappear hunt her for it.
about_author: Mara Fairweather is a former aviation-records analyst who writes thrillers about people erased by paperwork. She lives under no particular name in a coastal town she declines to identify.

chapters.title: Four Names, No Address
chapters.summary: Emrys Delacroix, working under her fourth identity, takes an unattributable case: a client wants proof his sister boarded Flight 447, which landed — but whose records have evaporated. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a life built on erasure, and the first crack of curiosity she can't delete.

chapters.title: The Flight That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Emrys confirms the impossible: air-traffic logs, booking data, and crew rosters for 447 were purged while the plane was airborne, yet it landed with 212 souls. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: professional dread hardening into personal obsession — someone with her old skills did this.

chapters.title: A Sister Who Doesn't Remember Flying
chapters.summary: Emrys finds the client's 'sister' alive, serene, and certain she's never been on a plane — her memories surgically smoothed. POV: Emrys, with a tense interview scene. Emotional beat: horror at the technology, and an unwelcome mirror of her own self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Clinic in the Fog
chapters.summary: The trail leads to Meridian Restorative Health, a discreet memory-editing network serving clients who need witnesses unmade. POV: Emrys, infiltrating as a grief-stricken relative. Emotional beat: claustrophobic fear as she recognizes the intake forms — she signed one once, she's sure.

chapters.title: What I Signed
chapters.summary: A stolen intake file shows Emrys's own handwriting and a name she buried: her original identity, and a consent form dated the night of the weapons transfer she once whistle-blew about. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: vertigo — she didn't just hide; she was edited.

chapters.title: The Handler's Call
chapters.summary: Emrys contacts her old intelligence handler, Voss, trading silence for access to Meridian's funding trail. POV: Voss, who reports the contact to someone above him. Emotional beat: the fragile, transactional trust between people who betray for a living.

chapters.title: Passenger Zero
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing the scrubbed flight, Emrys identifies the one passenger whose records were deleted hardest: Dr. Ilse Marchetti, Meridian's co-founder, apparently fleeing with proof of a weapons deal disguised as a medical shipment. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: grim triumph curdling — the flight was a kidnapping.

chapters.title: Tail Lights on the A12
chapters.summary: Emrys is made at a Meridian satellite site and runs a night pursuit through rain and traffic. POV: Emrys, intercut with her pursuer's cold professionalism. Emotional beat: adrenaline and a terrifying realization — they're herding her, not hunting her.

chapters.title: The Man Who Remembers Her
chapters.summary: A stranger, Callum Reeve, saves her from the trap — a Meridian technician whose own memory edits failed partially, leaving fragments of the weapons transfer. POV: Callum. Emotional beat: wary connection; two broken archives of a person recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Fragments of a Night
chapters.summary: Callum's残 fragments and Emrys's residual instincts piece together the transfer: a cargo of guidance modules moved under Meridian cover, bound for a strike someone wants to look accidental. POV: alternating Emrys and Callum. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in shared damage.

chapters.title: Voss's Ledger
chapters.summary: Emrys breaks into Voss's records and finds the operation's patron inside her former agency — the same people who once burned her as a whistle-blower. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: betrayal layered on betrayal; the past she fled was never behind her.

chapters.title: Ilse, Awake
chapters.summary: They locate Marchetti, half-wiped and hidden in a Meridian long-term care wing. In lucid minutes she reveals the attack's codeword: 'Clearance.' POV: Marchetti, disoriented and brave. Emotional beat: urgency — the wipe is scheduled to finish before she can testify.

chapters.title: Extraction in Daylight
chapters.summary: A brazen daytime extraction of Marchetti goes wrong; Callum is captured covering their escape. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: guilt and fury — she built the tradecraft that's now being used against her.

chapters.title: The Date on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Decoding Marchetti's cargo references, Emrys pins the attack: a freight flight over a coastal city, scheduled in 72 hours to fail 'accidentally' with the modules aboard. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: cold clarity — and the clock starting to scream.

chapters.title: Negotiating with a Ghost's Keeper
chapters.summary: Emrys confronts the Meridian director, who offers her original memories back in exchange for walking away. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: temptation — identity itself dangled as ransom; she almost says yes.

chapters.title: What Emrys Delacroix Knows
chapters.summary: She refuses, and in retaliation the director broadcasts her real name and face to every agency that wants her — burning her fourth identity. POV: Emrys, going dark in a stranger's apartment. Emotional beat: terror transforming into liberation; with nothing left to lose, she's finally free to act.

chapters.title: Breaking Callum Out
chapters.summary: Emrys raids the Meridian facility where Callum is held, using the clinic's own protocols against its staff. POV: Emrys and Callum. Emotional beat: fierce loyalty; the rescue doubles as reclaiming the skills that were stolen from her.

chapters.title: Clearance
chapters.summary: The team splits: Marchetti's evidence goes to a journalist, while Emrys boards the freight flight's ground crew rotation to reach the sabotaged modules before departure. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: controlled panic, the calm of someone finally all in one piece.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes on the Tarmac
chapters.summary: Emrys disables the guidance modules mid-pre-flight, is caught by the operation's field chief, and talks her way into a standoff as the departure clock runs out. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the climax's razor edge — identity as weapon: she names herself aloud to unnerve a man who only knows files.

chapters.title: The Accident That Didn't Happen
chapters.summary: The flight departs clean; the 'accident' window passes over an oblivious city. Voss, exposed by Marchetti's evidence, chooses a bullet over a trial. POV: Voss, then Emrys. Emotional beat: grim vindication and exhaustion.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Marchetti testifies; Meridian's network unravels publicly. Emrys, legally dead in four names, must decide whether to resurrect the fifth. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the quiet terror of becoming visible — and wanting to be.

chapters.title: A Contact for the Ghost
chapters.summary: Months later, Emrys signs her real name to her own whistle-blower account, publishes it, and waits for the knock — which comes as Callum at her door, alive and remembering. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: resolution — belonging chosen, identity claimed, memory hers at last.
